comment: This book is built by AI to describe distinct families and castles that share the name Rosenberg or its variations. Keep it concise and brief. Include information about each family, its members, and places related to it. Describe castles named Rosenberg in a separate section. Do not give detailed accounts of events or histories of specific people. Estates and Notable people keep simple. Dates in [YYYY] or [YYYY-YYYY] format

entries.title: Bauland and Odenwald Lords of Rosenberg

img.name: Coat of arms of the Baden/Odenwald Rosenbergs

entries.english: Recorded: [1276-1632]

Franconian lower-noble house of the Bauland, with an origin tradition linking it to Uissigheim. It acquired Boxberg and shifted its center there in 1381; its lands and offices spanned the Bauland and Schüpfergrund before the line ended in 1632.

entries.english: Recorded: [1270-1537]

Franconian ministerial family serving the bishops of Würzburg and associated with the cupbearer office. Its castle was known as Roßberg before becoming Schenkenschloss. Records use both Roßberg and Rosenberg forms for Schenk bearers.

entries.title: Mönch von Rosenberg
entries.english: Recorded: [1251-1679]

Lower-noble family recorded at Rosenberg from 1251, with holdings in the Bauland and a lordship at Mönchzell. Its members served the counts of Katzenelnbogen from 1354; records also document service in the Teutonic Order’s Prussian territories.

entries.english: Recorded: [1314-1359]

entries.english: Recorded: [1250-1611]

Witigon lords of South Bohemia, known in Latin and German records as de Rosis and von Rosenberg, and in Czech as z Rožmberka. They made Český Krumlov their principal seat and held lands in the Austrian Mühlviertel. Later family tradition connected the house with the Roman Orsini.

entries.title: Prussian
entries.english: Recorded: [1511-1954]

Courland-based noble house documented from the 16th century and later established in Prussia and Hesse. Otto Rosenberg presented a Moravian origin before the Courland Ritterbank in 1620; the Ritterbank recorded the family in 1631 after further evidence was presented. Russia recognized the family’s baronial title in 1863.

entries.subheading: Rosenberg Castle (Rosenburg am Kamp), Lower Austria
entries.english: Medieval castle in the Kamptal near Horn, later known as Rosenburg am Kamp. It served as the seat of local ministerial lords of Rosenberg; Goczwin is recorded in 1175 and Konrad in 1229.

Ruined hill castle on a Nagelfluh ridge above Burghalden, Herisau. Built in the 13th century, it served as the seat of a branch of the Rorschach-Rosenberg family and was burned during the Appenzell War in 1403; it was not rebuilt.

Ruins of a hill castle above Berneck, also called Bernang-Rosenberg. First recorded in 1210, it passed from the Lords of Bernang through the monastery of St Gallen to the Lords of Rosenberg; the castle buildings were sold for demolition in 1811.

Castle site on the Saale floodplain near its confluence with the Elbe. The royal estate is recorded in 965 and a castle in 1269; the Counts of Barby held it as a Magdeburg fief from 1306/08. It later became a Renaissance residence; surviving remains include the gate tower, parts of the enclosure, and vaulted cellars.

Vanished hilltop castle on the Schlossberg above Rosenberg in the Upper Palatinate. Probably built around 1100, it later became the Hofmark Rosenberg (1410) and declined from the 16th century; the keep stump is incorporated into the town war memorial.
Hilltop castle ruin above the village of Rosenberg, once held by the Lords of Vestenberg zu Rosenberg. The site retains earthworks, a moat, and a two-storey corner tower of sandstone.

Castle on a ridge above Riedenburg in the Altmühltal, probably built in the mid-12th century and transferred to Duke Ludwig I of Bavaria in 1196. It retains a Romanesque core with later Renaissance buildings and now houses a hunting museum and falconry centre.

Castle above the Vltava founded by Vok I of Rosenberg around the mid-13th century and documented in 1250. The Upper Castle was largely destroyed by fire in 1522; the Lower Castle was rebuilt in Renaissance style and later remodelled by the Buquoy family.

Bamberg episcopal stronghold first recorded in 1249. Medieval and early modern fortifications gave it a pentagonal form by 1699; the town acquired the fortress in 1888, and it now houses the Franconian Gallery.

Vanished castle at Schlossplatz in Rosenberg, now part of Buchen. The Mönch von Rosenberg held it in 1251, followed from the late 13th century by the Lords of Rosenberg. After the line ended in 1632, the estate passed to other noble houses; the last above-ground remains disappeared in 1926.
